 Description

 joshmedeski 
 opened on Sep 4, 2026 

 Issue body actions 

 Problem

 Benchmarks in this repo are already wired up for CI ( benchstat on PRs, the 
history dashboard on main ), but there is no way to see a before/after on my 
own machine. The local loop today is:

 just bench # scroll a wall of ns/op 
 # ...make changes... 
just bench # scroll a second wall, compare by eye 

 That works for one benchmark and falls apart across lister + picker at 
N = 10/100/1000. What I want locally is a committed baseline plus a 
 bar chart showing the gap between it and the current worktree — broad 
strokes, not every measurement.

 Desired workflow

 On main , on my Mac, run the suite once and save the result into the 
repo as the checked-in baseline.

 Open a worktree ( w/<n> , per the existing convention), make changes.

 Re-run the suite there.

 Get a TUI bar chart comparing worktree vs. baseline, one bar pair per 
benchmark, so a regression is visible without reading numbers.

 Roughly:

 just bench-baseline # on main: run and commit the baseline 
just bench-compare # in a worktree: run and chart against the baseline 

 Notes / open questions

 Baseline format. Raw go test -bench output is the honest thing to 
store, since benchstat can consume it directly and the parsing already 
exists in golang.org/x/perf/benchfmt . Something like 
 testdata/bench/baseline-darwin-arm64.txt , keyed by platform — a Mac 
baseline is not comparable to a Linux runner's, and committing one file that 
silently mixes both is worse than having none.

 Machine-specific baselines are a real caveat. A committed baseline is 
only meaningful on a comparable machine. It should record what produced it 
(Go version, GOOS/GOARCH, CPU model) and the chart should say so, rather 
than pretending a number from someone else's laptop is a target.

 Run parameters. Use -count=6 -benchtime=100ms to match what 
CONTRIBUTING.md already establishes as the point where these benchmarks hold 
to ±1%; anything looser makes the chart's deltas meaningless.

 Chart library. ntcharts 
builds on bubbletea + lipgloss , both already direct dependencies, and 
has a bar chart. That is the cheapest option in dependency terms. A plain 
 lipgloss -rendered bar row (no interactivity) would need no new dependency 
at all and might be enough for "broad strokes" — worth trying first.

 Where the code lives. Likely a cmd/ -style internal tool or a 
 just recipe wrapping a small Go program; it should not ship in the sesh 
binary itself.

 Show allocs too, or at least make it switchable. CONTRIBUTING.md's own 
advice is to trust allocs/op over time/op when they disagree, so a chart 
that only plots time invites exactly the misreading that doc warns about.

 Out of scope

 Replacing the CI benchstat job or the history dashboard. This is a local 
pre-push loop, not a gate.

 Failing on a threshold. Informational, same as CI is today.
